problem:
A triangle $S$ has vertices at $(-2,-3),(0,5),(2,-5).$ Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of ${S}^{′},$ the image of $S$ under the counterclockwise rotation ${R}_{\pi /2}$ by an angle of $\frac{\pi }{2}$ radians about the origin?

- $(3,-2)$
- $(-5,0)$
- $(5,2)$

feedback.problem:
A triangle $S$ has vertices at  $(0,2),(3,0),(0,0).$ Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of ${S}^{′},$ the image of $S$ under the **clockwise** rotation ${R}_{-{90}^{∘}}$ by an angle of ${90}^{∘}$ about the origin?

- $(0,-3)$
- $(0,0)$
- $(2,0)$
feedback.worked_solution:
The clockwise rotation ${R}_{-{90}^{∘}}$ by an angle of ${90}^{∘}$ is the same as counterclockwise rotation by an angle of ${270}^{∘}.$ It's given by the matrix

$$
R=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the image of $S$ under the action of ${R}_{-{90}^{∘}},$ we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $S:$

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under ${R}_{-{90}^{∘}}$ by calculating the matrix product $RX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}RX & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of ${S}^{′}$ are $(2,0),(0,-3),(0,0).$

So, the correct answer is "I, II, and III."
